caveats:
This product contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2020), processed by ESA and analyzed by the Earth Observatory of Singapore.

These are preliminary maps derived from satellite radar and should be used as guidance only. Coloured pixels may include false positives, and their absence does not mean an absence of damage or flooding.
dataset_source: NASA JPL-Caltech ARIA team; Earth Observatory of Singapore
methodology_other: Change detection on synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images acquired before and after the event. Damage Proxy Maps show significant changes in radar coherence and amplitude; Flood Proxy Maps show areas that changed to standing water. Maps are preliminary and checked against news reports and ground-level imagery where available.

notes:
# India Bangladesh Cyclone Amphan: Damage and Flood Proxy Maps, May 2020

The Advanced Rapid Imaging and Analysis (ARIA) team at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Caltech, in collaboration with the Earth Observatory of Singapore (EOS), produced these damage and flood proxy maps for India Bangladesh Cyclone Amphan (May 2020) from synthetic aperture radar (SAR) satellite images. Each map is a separate ZIP below with its GeoTIFF, a KMZ for Google Earth, the PNG figures and a text file describing how it was made and how to read it.

## Maps in this dataset

- **ARIA-SG Damage Proxy Map: India and Bangladesh, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4** (superseded)
- **ARIA-SG Damage Proxy Map: India and Bangladesh, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4** (superseded)
- **ARIA-SG Damage Proxy Map: Bangladesh and India, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4**
- **ARIA-SG Damage Proxy Map: Bangladesh and India, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4**
- **ARIA-SG Flood Proxy Map: India, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.8**
- **ARIA-SG Flood Proxy Map: India and Bangladesh, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4** (superseded)
- **ARIA-SG Flood Proxy Map: Bangladesh and India, Cyclone Amphan, 22 May 2020, v0.4** (superseded)

**More map details and files:** <https://sf.earthobservatory.sg/event/EOS_ARIA-SG_202005_India_Bangladesh_Cyclone_Amphan>

organization.description: The Earth Observatory of Singapore - Remote Sensing Lab (EOS-RS) is a research lab at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), Singapore. It uses satellite remote sensing, mainly synthetic aperture radar (SAR), to map natural hazards and disasters. The lab produces Damage Proxy Maps (DPMs) and Flood Proxy Maps (FPMs) showing where damage or flooding has likely occurred. Its work focuses on Southeast Asia and the wider Asia-Pacific, and it also responds to major disasters worldwide.
